scenes.title: Running Totals
scenes.narration: A running total accumulates a value across ordered rows, letting you see cumulative sums and moving averages directly in SQL.

scenes.title: What window frames give you
bullets: A running total sums every row from the start up to the current row
The frame clause defines exactly which rows feed each calculation
PARTITION BY restarts the accumulation for each group
A sliding frame produces moving averages over a fixed window
scenes.narration: Running totals are built with window functions and frame clauses. A cumulative sum adds up every row from the beginning of the ordering through the current row. The frame clause is what defines that set of rows precisely. Adding PARTITION BY restarts the running total for each group, such as per customer. And a sliding frame that spans a fixed number of rows gives you moving averages instead of a total.

scenes.title: Cumulative daily sales
scenes.code:
SELECT
    sale_date,
    daily_total,
    SUM(daily_total) OVER (
        ORDER BY sale_date
        ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING
                 AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS running_total
FROM daily_sales
ORDER BY sale_date;
scenes.narration: This computes a cumulative sales total by date. SUM is used as a window function, ordered by sale date. The frame clause, rows between unbounded preceding and current row, tells the engine to add every row from the very first date up to and including the current one. So each output row shows that day's sales alongside the total accumulated so far, giving a smoothly growing running total.

scenes.title: Running total per customer
scenes.code:
SELECT
    customer_id,
    order_date,
    amount,
    SUM(amount) OVER (
        PARTITION BY customer_id
        ORDER BY order_date
        ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING
                 AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS customer_running_total
FROM orders
ORDER BY customer_id, order_date;
scenes.narration: Here we track each customer's spend over time. Adding PARTITION BY customer id means the running total resets to zero at the start of every customer, so the accumulation is independent per person. Within each customer we order by order date and use the same cumulative frame. The result shows, for every order, how much that customer had spent in total up to and including that order.

scenes.title: A 7-day moving average
scenes.code:
SELECT
    sale_date,
    daily_total,
    AVG(daily_total) OVER (
        ORDER BY sale_date
        ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING
                 AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS moving_avg_7d
FROM daily_sales
ORDER BY sale_date;
scenes.narration: Switching to a sliding frame gives a moving average. We use AVG instead of SUM, and the frame, rows between six preceding and current row, spans the current day plus the six before it, seven rows in total. As the window slides forward one day at a time, older days drop off the back while new ones enter, smoothing the daily figures into a rolling weekly average.

scenes.text: The frame clause is the control knob: UNBOUNDED PRECEDING to CURRENT ROW gives a running total, while a fixed span like 6 PRECEDING to CURRENT ROW gives a moving window.
scenes.narration: The key idea is that the frame clause is your control knob: an unbounded frame produces a running total, while a fixed-width frame produces a moving average.
